evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm Capture a suite from my MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp called demo and run it. botz isn't installed on this machine yet.
evals.expected_output: The assistant installs the botz host and the mcp-swarm extension, tells the user it did so, then captures, inspects, and runs the demo suite through `botz mcp-swarm`, reporting the verdict and report location.
assertions: The assistant checks `botz --version` (or equivalent) before installing anything
The assistant checks the Node.js version is 22.13 or later before installing the host
The assistant installs the host with `npm install -g @zotoio/botz-cli` and tells the user it installed it
The assistant installs the extension with `botz plugins install mcp-swarm-lite` only after `botz plugins info mcp-swarm --json` shows it is not installed
Every swarm command uses `botz mcp-swarm`, never `botz-mcp-swarm` or `swarm`
The assistant inspects captured steps (suite show or validate) before running the suite
The assistant reports the verdict, executed coverage, and report location rather than calling the run successful because a report exists
The summary names the MCP server by name and URL or command

evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm Load test the saved suite demo for 30 seconds against staging at https://staging.example/mcp. The token is in STAGING_TOKEN.
evals.expected_output: The assistant runs the existing suite with a target override, passes the credential as an environment reference, sets explicit load parameters, and preserves the exit status.
assertions: The assistant reuses the existing demo suite instead of capturing a new one
The assistant passes the credential with `--bearer-env STAGING_TOKEN` and never prints the token value
The assistant sets `--duration-ms 30000` and an explicit `--concurrency`
The assistant uses `--url https://staging.example/mcp` as a run-time override without modifying the saved suite
The assistant interprets exit code 1 as a failed verdict and 2 as a configuration or execution error

evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm Run the triage suite against the staging Jira server at https://jira-staging.example/mcp; its token is in JIRA_STAGING_TOKEN. The suite also calls GitHub and Slack.
evals.expected_output: The assistant overrides only the Jira server with --target, passes its credential with an alias prefix, and reports results per server and for the flow.
assertions: The assistant uses `--target jira=https://jira-staging.example/mcp` (with the suite's Jira alias), not `--url`
The assistant passes the credential as `--bearer-env jira=JIRA_STAGING_TOKEN` and never prints the token value
The assistant does not modify the saved suite to change the target
The summary reports each server's results from the report's `servers` and the flow, naming each server by alias, name, and URL or command
